summary: An excerpt from a fiction novel (Book 1, part 195) in which the narrator visits Darryl in a hospital room after he woke crying and was given sedatives; the narrator notices his chewed nails, recalls his childhood, and holds his hand, nearly saying 'I love you'. The narrator also recounts a plea deal in which charges of electronic terrorism and inciting riots were dropped in exchange for a guilty plea to petty theft, resulting in three months in a day-release program at a Mission District halfway house. The excerpt closes with Marcus being told that Carrie Johnstone is being cleared by a closed military tribunal and returned to duty, and with the Feds disputing the Governor's shutdown of the Treasure Island facility.
one_line: Fiction excerpt where Marcus visits the sedated Darryl in hospital, then describes his plea deal and a day-release program, and news of Carrie Johnstone's tribunal and the Treasure Island shutdown.
key_facts: Darryl wakes up crying and cannot stop, and the staff gave him something to help him sleep.
Darryl had a semi-private hospital room, and an older Arab-looking man in his 40s occupied the other bed.
The narrator realizes the man in the other bed is the guy he was chained to on the way off Treasure Island.
Darryl had been a nail-biter as a kid but kicked the habit when the group reached high school.
The narrator believes Van talked Darryl out of nail-biting by pointing out how gross it was.
The narrator says 'Hey, D, you made it. You're going to be OK' to the sleeping Darryl.
Barbara called the narrator at the office on July 4th weekend.
The narrator was the only one whose excuse for working the holiday weekend was that his day-release program would not let him leave town.
The narrator was convicted of stealing Masha's phone.
The prosecution dropped charges of 'Electronic terrorism' and 'inciting riots' in a deal with the narrator's lawyer.
In exchange, the narrator pleaded guilty to misdemeanor petty theft.
The narrator received three months in a day-release program with a halfway house for juvenile offenders in the Mission.
Carrie Johnstone was cleared of wrongdoing by a closed military tribunal, and the file is sealed.
Carrie Johnstone is being returned to active duty; her name came out in preliminary hearings at the California Superior Court.
The Feds called the Governor's shut-down of the Treasure Island facility 'unilateral, illegal'.
